title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure, and the impersonated party is the product. An AI-generated video presented a well-known financial sector figure as the face of an investment, and that fabricated endorsement did the work of making the offer believable. The synthetic media was not the target of the fraud, it was the instrument, and the thing it counterfeited was a person's identity and presumed judgement.

The failure sits at the first point of contact, the advertisement itself, and it is there that any check would have had to happen. Verifying independently who the victim was dealing with, and confirming Financial Conduct Authority authorisation for the investment, are the two checks the police identified as the ones that were missing. Everything after that first contact, the WhatsApp messages, the help setting up accounts, the remote access to the computer, the pressure to borrow, is ordinary fraud tradecraft that the video had already bought entry for.

What is not established: the celebrity is not named, no arrest or charge is reported, the tool that produced the video is unidentified, and the £250,000 loss rests on a police account rather than a court finding. The BBC's sighting of separate scams using named financial experts is not a finding that any of them appeared in this one.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area lost £250,000 after an AI generated video scam. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim saw a fake video that appeared to feature a well known financial sector personality. It advertised an investment with claimed significant returns. The victim first invested a small amount, then was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more. Fraudsters helped create multiple online accounts and got remote access to the victim's computer, saying they were assisting with the investment.

The PSNI called it a complex and large fraud. It said the criminals built trust and pushed the victim to borrow money, with funds sent to accounts they controlled. Police did not name the celebrity, though BBC News NI has seen scams using financial experts Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. Police advised people to independently verify who they deal with and check Financial Conduct Authority authorisation. Superintendent Joanne Gibson of the Scamwise Partnership urged people to pause and verify and families to discuss fraud.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
